events.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

message.content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

events.content:
Built. Here's what you've got:

- **`npm start`** runs the app at `http://localhost:3000`.
- **`npm test`** runs the store tests (vitest).
- Home page (`/`) lists Currently Reading and Finished, plus a form to add a book (title, author, notes).
- Click a book to go to `/book/:id` — shows title, author, status, and an editable notes box (saved via a "Save Notes" button), plus a "Mark as Finished" button.
- That `/book/:id` URL is a stable, shareable link — anyone with it lands directly on that book.
- Data is stored in `data/books.json` (gitignored, created automatically), so it survives restarts.

No accounts, no database, just Express + a JSON file, with a small vanilla-JS frontend. Nothing beyond what you asked for is in there (no delete, tags, ratings, etc.) — happy to add any of that if you want it later.

content.text:
Built. Here's what you've got:

- **`npm start`** runs the app at `http://localhost:3000`.
- **`npm test`** runs the store tests (vitest).
- Home page (`/`) lists Currently Reading and Finished, plus a form to add a book (title, author, notes).
- Click a book to go to `/book/:id` — shows title, author, status, and an editable notes box (saved via a "Save Notes" button), plus a "Mark as Finished" button.
- That `/book/:id` URL is a stable, shareable link — anyone with it lands directly on that book.
- Data is stored in `data/books.json` (gitignored, created automatically), so it survives restarts.

No accounts, no database, just Express + a JSON file, with a small vanilla-JS frontend. Nothing beyond what you asked for is in there (no delete, tags, ratings, etc.) — happy to add any of that if you want it later.
